subject: Emotions
title: Love as a Practice
description: A short lesson to help you apply Love as a Practice.

hook.text: Fromm said love isn't something you fall into—it's something you practice, like playing piano or learning a language.

buildup.text: In 'The Art of Loving,' Fromm argued modern culture treats love as luck. Love is a skill needing discipline and effort.

discovery.text: Research supports this: long-happy couples call love a verb, not a noun. They do loving things during unloving moments.

twist.text: The fairy tale model—find the right person and love is effortless—sets everyone up for failure when effort is required.

climax.text: Love as practice means choosing someone repeatedly, not once. Every morning is a renewal, not an assumption.

punchline.text: Love isn't a feeling you have. It's a thing you do.

quiz.question: What did Erich Fromm argue about love?
